cards.front: What should you know about static electricity?
cards.back: A build-up of electric charge on the surface of an insulating material. It is caused by friction between two insulators — electrons are transferred from one material to the other.

cards.front: What should you know about electric field?
cards.back: A region around a charged object where another charged object experiences a force. Field lines point from positive to negative charges.

cards.front: What should you know about sparking?
cards.back: When the potential difference between a charged object and the earth (or another object) is large enough, electrons can jump across the gap, creating a spark.

cards.front: What should you know about by friction?
cards.back: When two insulating materials are rubbed together, electrons are transferred from one to the other. The material that gains electrons becomes negatively charged . The material that loses electrons becomes positively charged .

cards.front: What should you know about like charges repel. unlike charges attract.?
cards.back: Two positive charges repel; two negative charges repel; a positive and negative charge attract.

cards.front: What should you know about electric field?
cards.back: The region around a charged object where a force is exerted on other charged objects. The field is strongest close to the charge.

cards.front: What should you know about sparking occurs?
cards.back: when the potential difference between a charged object and the earth (or another conductor) is large enough to make electrons jump across the gap. The air is ionised, allowing current to flow briefly.

cards.front: What should you know about earthing?
cards.back: prevents dangerous static build-up by providing a conducting path to the ground, allowing charge to flow away safely.

cards.front: Recall a key point about P8 Static Electricity
cards.back: While there is little numerical maths in static electricity, you must be able to interpret electric field diagrams quantitatively. The spacing of field lines indicates field strength — closer lines mean a stronger field. Charge is quantised: all charges are whole-number multiples of the electron charge (e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C). When electrons transfer, the charge on each object is equal and opposite (conservation of charge).

cards.front: What should you know about answers?
cards.back: (a) Lower humidity means drier air, so charge cannot leak away through moisture in the air — static builds up more easily. The data shows more incidents in dry winter conditions (8/month) and fewer in humid summer (2/month). Installing humidifiers reduced incidents to 1/month, confirming the relationship. (b) Earthing the metal vats is more effective because it directly eliminates charge build-up on the vats (the most likely source of a spark near flammable solvent). Anti-static overalls prevent charge on workers but do not address charge on the vats and pipes where the solvent is located. Bot
